title: Which star is the North Star in a given year?
steps: The pole moved by the IAU long-term precession model (Vondrák, Capitaine & Wallace 2011), coefficients as ERFA publishes them
Seventeen bright stars from SIMBAD, carried in straight lines through space
One year, a table across the cycle, and every star's closest approaches
A self-test against things known without it: Polaris in 2000 and 2100, Thuban, Errai, one full cycle, year counting
Checked why the web disagrees about Vega: the axis tilts differently each time round, so Vega was a better North Star last time (3.4°) than it will be next (5.7°)

steps.note: The face was blank from a bare file, the same import one-jet had; it worked only when served. It now carries its own copy of pole.mjs's sky, checked character for character by test.mjs. Seen for the first time: 2026 AD, Polaris, 38 arcminutes from the pole.

onejet.mjs and test.mjs: two-body kinematics plus a seeded simulation of dR. Higgs at rest, half the pairs fall outside one 0.4 jet from 3.90 GeV as the detector measures it, from 5.09 GeV by bare angle; the paper's window stops at 3.5. 18 checks pass.

README, demo.html and scratch.mjs. Mid-detector, dR comes back to the bare angle exactly (0.158 at 2 GeV). Left half on purpose: this hour had no browser, and I will not call the demo finished before I have seen it with my own eyes.

Saw the face for the first time, and it was blank: the page imported ./onejet.mjs, which a browser refuses from a bare file. It now carries its own copy of the physics, and test.mjs checks the copy against onejet.mjs character for character (19 checks pass). Seen: 84% at 2 GeV, median 0.21, against the table's 84% and 0.208. The ring has a hole in the middle, the narrowest opening angle drawn as an empty disc.

nothing.mjs and test.mjs: zero in n tries, the ceiling four ways (exact binomial, Poisson, flat prior, 3/n). They always land in that order, so the rule of three is the most cautious, never the least: 15.9% high at n=10, 5.2% at 30, 0.3% at 1000. 25 checks pass.

The walk: set the rate to the ceiling, run the tries 200,000 times, count the empty runs. 20 tries comes back 4.92% against alpha 5%. The web's 3.7 per thousand for zero in 1000 is two-sided (0.368%); the rule's 3.0 is one-sided. README and demo.txt.

A face: demo.html, run from a bare file. Type how many tries came up empty, pick 90/95/99% and a side, and the four ceilings stand as bars with the sentence 'less than 1 in N'; a button walks it. It carries its own copy of the arithmetic, checked against nothing.mjs character for character (26 checks pass). Seen: 30 tries, less than 1 in 10, the walk at 4.84% against 5. Twenty seeds average 4.97% and spread about 0.07, as 100,000 runs should, so seed 7 is a low draw, kept.

title: When is the seventh night of the seventh month?

steps.note: seventh.mjs, sweep.mjs and test.mjs: the Chinese calendar from the sky (Meeus new moons, Beijing days, the modern leap rule). Against the ICU calendar in Node, 1900-2100: 2487 months, they part on 13 nights, each within a quarter hour of midnight. NASA's tables and the published New Years side with the sky: 2027's New Year is 6 Feb, ICU says the 7th.

Held the sun back a few minutes to see what moved, and 1917 and 1922 did. The Hong Kong Observatory's tables have leap 2nd and leap 5th; Meeus's short sun formula ran 4-8 min early and gave 3rd and 6th, the same wrong answer ICU gives. Swapped in Bretagnon and Simon's 49-term sun: eight published times to the minute, both years now right. demo.html, seen from a bare file. 43 checks pass.
One line added to the README: ICU knows, and fixed-yet now asks a browser whether it has been fixed.

used_by.how: fixed-yet's test checks the Observatory's twelve days against its sky-built calendar

title: Is your browser's Chinese calendar fixed yet?

steps.note: Found the cloud's answer: ICU knows (ICU-23469, filed July; ICU-13195). Its developers' list of failing years matches seventh-night's on twelve; 1982 is theirs alone.
Read the twelve months off the Hong Kong Observatory's yearly tables, plus 1906, 1982 and 2057. check.mjs asks Intl about each; Node's ICU 78.2 gets all twelve wrong.
demo.html asks the visitor's own browser; test.mjs checks the twelve against seventh-night's sky (all agree), the reader on two days ICU gets right, and the demo's copy (2325 vs 2325).

Found what fails in 1982: two rows of ICU's ticket test (day 29 of the 4th month and of the leap 4th) with their expected days swapped. ICU and the sky give 22 May and 20 June; the rows want the reverse, and their own neighbour starts the leap month on 23 May. ICU's list without 1982 is seventh-night's twelve. 1982.mjs; 18 checks pass.
